q.q: Which international financial institution provides low-interest loans, zero-to-low-interest credits, and grants to developing countries?
q.x: The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions working for sustainable solutions that reduce poverty and build shared prosperity in developing countries.

q.q: Which international organization oversees the global standard for civil aviation?
q.x: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is a UN specialized agency that develops standards and recommended practices for international civil aviation. It is headquartered in Montreal, Canada. Its goal is to ensure the safe and orderly growth of international civil aviation.

q.q: Which organization's primary objective is to promote international monetary cooperation and provide policy advice and technical assistance to its member countries?
q.x: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) works to foster global monetary cooperation, secure financial stability, and facilitate international trade. It also provides loans to help member countries address balance-of-payments problems.

q.q: The headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) is located in which city?
q.x: The World Health Organization is a specialized agency of the UN responsible for international public health. It is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. It coordinates global responses to health emergencies.

q.q: Which organization was established by the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944 alongside the IMF?
q.x: The Bretton Woods Conference of 1944 led to the creation of the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), which is the core of the World Bank Group. The IMF was created at the same conference to monitor international currency exchange rates.

q.q: Which of these organizations is headquartered in New Delhi, India?
q.x: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) is an alliance of countries initiated by India. Its headquarters is located in Gurugram, near New Delhi. It focuses on the efficient consumption of solar energy.

q.q: Where is the secretariat of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) located?
q.x: SAARC was founded in 1985 in Dhaka, but its permanent secretariat was established in Kathmandu, Nepal in 1987. It promotes economic and regional integration among South Asian countries.

q.q: Which international organization is known for its work in protecting children's rights worldwide?
q.x: UNICEF stands for the United Nations Children's Fund. It provides humanitarian and developmental assistance to children and mothers in developing countries. It is headquartered in New York City.

q.q: Which international organization is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, and is responsible for international public health?
q.x: The World Health Organization (WHO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health. It is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. The organization was established on 7 April 1948.

q.q: The 'New Development Bank' (NDB), formerly known as the BRICS Development Bank, has its headquarters in which city?
q.x: The New Development Bank is a multilateral development bank established by the BRICS states (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa). Its headquarters is located in Shanghai, China.

q.q: Which organization is responsible for promoting international cooperation in education, science, and culture?
q.x: UNESCO stands for the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization. It aims to promote world peace and security through international cooperation in educational, scientific, and cultural reforms.

q.q: The 'Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries' (OPEC) has its headquarters in:
q.x: OPEC is a permanent intergovernmental organization of petroleum-exporting nations. Although it consists largely of Middle Eastern countries, its headquarters have been located in Vienna, Austria, since 1965.

q.q: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) was established primarily as a:
q.x: NATO is an intergovernmental military alliance between 32 member states. It was established in 1949 to provide collective security against potential threats.

q.q: The headquarters of the International Solar Alliance (ISA), an intergovernmental organization launched by India and France, is located in which city?
q.x: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) is headquartered in Gurugram, India. It was launched at the India Africa Summit and the UN Climate Change Conference in Paris in 2015. It aims to work for efficient consumption of solar energy to reduce dependence on fossil fuels.

q.q: Which international organization is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, and is responsible for international public health, including the coordination of responses to global pandemics?
q.x: The World Health Organization (WHO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health. It is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. Its primary role is to direct and coordinate international health work.

q.q: Which UN agency is specifically dedicated to the welfare of children globally?
q.x: UNICEF, or the United Nations Children's Fund, provides humanitarian and developmental assistance to children worldwide. It was created in 1946 to help children in the aftermath of World War II.

q.q: Which international organization is responsible for setting international standards for food safety, labeling, and quality through the 'Codex Alimentarius'?
q.x: The Codex Alimentarius Commission was established by FAO and WHO to develop food standards, guidelines, and codes of practice. These contribute to the safety, quality, and fairness of international food trade.

q.q: Which organization is primarily focused on the protection of children's rights worldwide?
q.x: UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund) is a UN agency responsible for providing humanitarian and developmental aid to children worldwide. It operates in over 190 countries.

q.q: Which organization oversees the rules of international trade between nations?
q.x: The World Trade Organization (WTO) deals with the global rules of trade between nations. Its main function is to ensure that trade flows as smoothly, predictably, and freely as possible.

q.q: Which of the following is the headquarters of the International Olympic Committee (IOC)?
q.x: The International Olympic Committee is the governing body for the Olympic Games. It is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland. It organizes the modern Olympic Games held every four years.

q.q: The 'Asian Development Bank' (ADB) has its headquarters located in which city?
q.x: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) is a regional development bank established in 1966. It is headquartered in the Ortigas Center located in Mandaluyong, Metro Manila, Philippines. It aims to promote social and economic development in Asia.

q.q: Which of the following bodies is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, located at the Peace Palace in The Hague?
q.x: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is the principal judicial organ of the UN. It is the only one of the six principal organs of the UN not located in New York. It settles legal disputes submitted by States.

q.q: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), which promotes the peaceful use of nuclear energy, is headquartered in which city?
q.x: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is an international organization that seeks to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy and to inhibit its use for any military purpose. Its headquarters are in Vienna, Austria.

q.q: What is the primary objective of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC)?
o: Promoting regional cooperation and technological collaboration
q.x: BIMSTEC is an international organization of seven nations of South Asia and Southeast Asia. Its primary goal is to foster regional cooperation and accelerate economic growth among member states. It focuses on sectors like trade, technology, and connectivity.

q.q: What is the primary objective of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), an intergovernmental organization established in 1989?
o: To promote international trade and investment
To combat money laundering and terrorist financing
To provide low-interest loans to developing nations
q.x: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is an intergovernmental organization that designs and promotes policies and standards to combat money laundering and terrorist financing. It was established by the G7 in 1989.

q.q: Which organization's primary objective is to promote international monetary cooperation and secure financial stability?
q.x: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) works to foster global monetary cooperation, secure financial stability, and facilitate international trade. It is a key global financial institution.

q.q: What is the primary role of the 'Financial Action Task Force' (FATF)?
o: Combating money laundering and terror financing
Setting interest rates for member nations
q.x: The FATF is an intergovernmental organization founded in 1989 on the initiative of the G7 to develop policies to combat money laundering. It has since expanded its mandate to include the combatting of terrorist financing and proliferation financing.

q.q: Who is the current parent organization of the World Health Organization (WHO)?
q.x: The World Health Organization is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health. It is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

q.q: What is the primary objective of the organization known as OPEC?
o: Coordination of petroleum policies among member countries
q.x: OPEC stands for the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries. Its mission is to coordinate and unify the petroleum policies of its member countries to ensure the stabilization of oil markets.

q.q: What does the acronym 'ASEAN' stand for?
o: Association of South East Asian Nations
Alliance of South East African Nations
Association of South European Asian Nations
Agency of South East Asian Networks
q.x: ASEAN is a regional intergovernmental organization comprising ten countries in Southeast Asia. It promotes intergovernmental cooperation and facilitates economic, political, and security integration.

q.q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations (UN) located?
q.x: The United Nations is an international organization founded in 1945. Its primary headquarters is situated in New York City, USA. It serves as the main hub for global diplomacy.

q.q: What is the primary function of the International Labour Organization (ILO)?
q.x: The ILO is a United Nations agency whose mandate is to advance social and economic justice by setting international labor standards. It was established in 1919 and is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

q.q: Which global organization is responsible for the 'Red List of Threatened Species'?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
q.x: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) maintains the IUCN Red List, which is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of plant and animal species.

q.q: Which international body is responsible for the 'Red List' of threatened species?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)
q.x: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, established in 1964, is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of plant and animal species. The IUCN is an international organization working in the field of nature conservation and sustainable use of natural resources.

q.q: Which organization is tasked with the 'protection of refugees' and the resolution of refugee problems worldwide?
q.x: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) is a UN agency mandated to aid and protect refugees, forcibly displaced communities, and stateless people. It was established in 1950.

q.q: Which body serves as the permanent secretariat for the G20, the premier forum for international economic cooperation?
q.x: The G20 does not have a permanent secretariat. Its presidency rotates annually among its members, and the host country is responsible for the administrative tasks and summit organization for that year.

q.q: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is located in which of the following cities?
q.x: The World Trade Organization deals with the global rules of trade between nations. Its headquarters are located in Geneva, Switzerland.

q.q: The headquarters of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) is located in which country?
q.x: The International Olympic Committee is a non-governmental sports organization based in Lausanne, Switzerland. It is the authority responsible for the modern Olympic Games.

q.q: Which organization is responsible for setting global standards for food and agriculture?
q.x: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations. It leads international efforts to defeat hunger and improve nutrition and food security. Its headquarters is in Rome, Italy.

q.q: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the G7 (Group of Seven)?
q.x: The G7 consists of Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States. India is not a member of the G7, although it is often invited as a guest participant to summits.

q.q: Which of the following countries is NOT a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council?
q.x: The permanent members of the UN Security Council (P5) are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Germany is not a permanent member, though it frequently serves as an elected non-permanent member.

q.q: Where is the headquarters of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) located?
q.x: The International Court of Justice is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations. It is located at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands. It settles legal disputes between states.

q.q: The headquarters of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is situated in:
q.x: The International Court of Justice is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations. It is located in the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands. It is the only UN principal organ not located in New York.

q.q: Which organization manages the 'Red List of Threatened Species', which is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of biological species?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
q.x: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, founded in 1964, is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of plant and animal species. The IUCN is headquartered in Gland, Switzerland.

q.q: The headquarters of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is located in which city?
q.x: The International Court of Justice is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations and is located at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands. It is the only one of the six principal organs of the UN not located in New York City.

q.q: Which organization is known as the 'Bank for Central Banks' and is located in Basel, Switzerland?
q.x: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) is an international financial institution owned by central banks that 'fosters international monetary and financial cooperation'. It is often referred to as the bank for central banks.

q.q: Which organization is responsible for setting international standards for aviation safety?
q.x: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations. It coordinates the principles and techniques of international air navigation.

q.q: Which international financial institution is headquartered in Washington, D.C.?
q.x: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank are both headquartered in Washington, D.C. These institutions focus on global monetary cooperation and economic development.

q.q: Which international organization governs the rules of trade between nations and serves as a forum for trade negotiations?
o: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
q.x: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is the only global international organization dealing with the rules of trade between nations. It operates on the principle of trade negotiations and dispute settlement mechanisms.

q.q: Which organization is primarily responsible for international monetary cooperation and financial stability?
q.x: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) oversees the global monetary system. It provides policy advice and financing to members in economic difficulty. Its headquarters is in Washington, D.C.

q.q: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) is a:
q.x: NATO is an intergovernmental military alliance between 32 member states. It is based on the North Atlantic Treaty signed in 1949. Its headquarters is located in Brussels, Belgium.

q.q: Which organization focuses on the promotion of education, science, and culture?
q.x: UNESCO stands for the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization. It aims to promote world peace and security through international cooperation. Its headquarters is in Paris, France.

q.q: What is the primary objective of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
q.x: The WTO deals with the global rules of trade between nations. Its main function is to ensure that trade flows as smoothly, predictably, and freely as possible. It is based in Geneva, Switzerland.

q.q: The 'ASEAN' regional intergovernmental organization consists of member states primarily located in which part of the world?
q.x: ASEAN stands for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. It was established on 8 August 1967 in Bangkok, Thailand, and consists of ten member countries in Southeast Asia.

q.q: The 'ASEAN' organization consists of member nations located primarily in which region?
q.x: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is a regional grouping that promotes economic, political, and security cooperation among its ten members in Southeast Asia.

q.q: Which organization releases the 'World Happiness Report' annually?
q.x: The World Happiness Report is a publication of the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network. It uses data from the Gallup World Poll to rank countries based on self-reported happiness. It has been published since 2012.

q.q: Where is the permanent headquarters of the SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) Secretariat located?
q.x: The SAARC Secretariat was established in Kathmandu, Nepal, on 16 January 1987. Its purpose is to promote the welfare of the peoples of South Asia and to improve their quality of life.
